lines.text: Nine lights, each on or off.
lines.caption: Nine lights, each on or off.

lines.text: Count each row and column alone, and you get three hundred eighty-four. Too many!
lines.caption: Count each row and column alone, and you get three hundred eighty-four. Too many!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's learn to count overlaps without counting twice.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's learn to count overlaps without counting twice.

lines.text: Each light in a three by three grid of nine lights is on or off.
lines.caption: Each light in a three by three grid of nine lights is on or off.

lines.text: How many on and off patterns have at least one full row, or at least one full column, of lights on?
lines.caption: How many on and off patterns have at least one full row, or at least one full column, of lights on?

lines.text: Here are the choices.
lines.caption: Here are the choices.

lines.text: A pattern wins if some row is all on, or some column is all on. Or both!
lines.caption: A pattern wins if some row is all on, or some column is all on. Or both!

lines.text: Each light has two choices. So there are two to the ninth, five hundred twelve patterns in all.
lines.caption: Each light has two choices. So there are two to the ninth, five hundred twelve patterns in all.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's count the losers: patterns with no full row and no full column.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's count the losers: patterns with no full row and no full column.

lines.text: Start with rows. One row of three lights has two times two times two, eight patterns.
lines.caption: Start with rows. One row of three lights has two times two times two, eight patterns.

lines.text: Only one of those eight is all on. So each row has seven safe choices.
lines.caption: Only one of those eight is all on. So each row has seven safe choices.

lines.text: Seven times seven times seven. That's three hundred forty-three patterns with no full row.
lines.caption: Seven times seven times seven. That's three hundred forty-three patterns with no full row.

lines.text: But some of those still have a full column. Let's find them.
lines.caption: But some of those still have a full column. Let's find them.

lines.text: Say column one is full. Then every row has its first light on.
lines.caption: Say column one is full. Then every row has its first light on.

lines.text: The other two can't both be on, or that row is full. That leaves three choices per row.
lines.caption: The other two can't both be on, or that row is full. That leaves three choices per row.

lines.text: Three times three times three is twenty-seven. Each column gives twenty-seven, so eighty-one.
lines.caption: Three times three times three is twenty-seven. Each column gives twenty-seven, so eighty-one.

lines.text: Careful! Patterns with two full columns, third column off, got counted twice.
lines.caption: Careful! Patterns with two full columns, third column off, got counted twice.

lines.text: So subtract each one once. There are three.
lines.caption: So subtract each one once. There are three.

lines.text: Three full columns would fill the rows, so they never appear. Eighty-one minus three: seventy-eight.
lines.caption: Three full columns would fill the rows, so they never appear. Eighty-one minus three: seventy-eight.

lines.text: So the losers are three hundred forty-three minus seventy-eight. That's two hundred sixty-five.
lines.caption: So the losers are three hundred forty-three minus seventy-eight. That's two hundred sixty-five.

lines.text: Those are the patterns with NO full row or column. That's not our answer yet!
lines.caption: Those are the patterns with NO full row or column. That's not our answer yet!

lines.text: Take them from all five hundred twelve.
lines.caption: Take them from all five hundred twelve.

lines.text: Five hundred twelve minus two hundred sixty-five is <short pause> two hundred forty-seven! Choice B.
lines.caption: Five hundred twelve minus two hundred sixty-five is two hundred forty-seven! Choice B.

lines.text: Now a second way: inclusion and exclusion. Each row or column gets its own group of patterns.
lines.caption: Now a second way: inclusion and exclusion. Each row or column gets its own group of patterns.

lines.text: Fix one row or column all on. The other six lights are free. Two to the sixth power is sixty-four.
lines.caption: Fix one row or column all on. The other six lights are free. Two to the sixth power is sixty-four.

lines.text: Six of them, sixty-four each, is three hundred eighty-four. But overlaps got counted more than once!
lines.caption: Six of them, sixty-four each, is three hundred eighty-four. But overlaps got counted more than once!

lines.text: So subtract each pair. Two rows, or two columns, leave three free lights: eight patterns.
lines.caption: So subtract each pair. Two rows, or two columns, leave three free lights: eight patterns.

lines.text: A row and a column make a cross of five lights. Four are free, so sixteen patterns.
lines.caption: A row and a column make a cross of five lights. Four are free, so sixteen patterns.

lines.text: Six row or column pairs give forty-eight. Three times three crosses give one hundred forty-four.
lines.caption: Six row or column pairs give forty-eight. Three times three crosses give one hundred forty-four.

lines.text: A pattern in three groups was added three times, then taken away three times.
lines.caption: A pattern in three groups was added three times, then taken away three times.

lines.text: That's zero! So add the triples back.
lines.caption: That's zero! So add the triples back.

lines.text: Two rows and a column light seven lights. Two are free: four patterns. Nine such groups: thirty-six.
lines.caption: Two rows and a column light seven lights. Two are free: four patterns. Nine such groups: thirty-six.

lines.text: A row and two columns give thirty-six more. Plus all rows, and all columns. That's seventy-four.
lines.caption: A row and two columns give thirty-six more. Plus all rows, and all columns. That's seventy-four.

lines.text: Keep flipping signs. Two rows and two columns leave one free light. Nine ways, times two: eighteen.
lines.caption: Keep flipping signs. Two rows and two columns leave one free light. Nine ways, times two: eighteen.

lines.text: Three rows and a column, or a row and three columns, light everything. Six more: twenty-four.
lines.caption: Three rows and a column, or a row and three columns, light everything. Six more: twenty-four.

lines.text: Groups of five, and all six, light every light. That's six, and then one.
lines.caption: Groups of five, and all six, light every light. That's six, and then one.

lines.text: Put it together. Three hundred eighty-four minus one hundred ninety-two, plus seventy-four, minus twenty-four, plus six, minus one. That's two hundred forty-seven again!
lines.caption: Put it together. Three hundred eighty-four minus one hundred ninety-two, plus seventy-four, minus twenty-four, plus six, minus one. That's two hundred forty-seven again!

lines.text: When would you pick this one? Here, counting losers is shorter. But this works for ANY overlaps.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? Here, counting losers is shorter. But this works for ANY overlaps.

lines.text: Choice A, one hundred sixty-nine, is just the full rows.
lines.caption: Choice A, one hundred sixty-nine, is just the full rows.

lines.text: Choice C, two hundred sixty-five, is the losers. You forgot to subtract from five hundred twelve.
lines.caption: Choice C, two hundred sixty-five, is the losers. You forgot to subtract from five hundred twelve.

lines.text: Choice D, three hundred thirty-eight, is one hundred sixty-nine for rows, plus the same for columns.
lines.caption: Choice D, three hundred thirty-eight, is one hundred sixty-nine for rows, plus the same for columns.

lines.text: Patterns with both get counted twice.
lines.caption: Patterns with both get counted twice.

lines.text: E, three hundred eighty-four, is six times sixty-four, with no overlaps taken away.
lines.caption: E, three hundred eighty-four, is six times sixty-four, with no overlaps taken away.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. When groups overlap, ask: did I count anything twice?
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. When groups overlap, ask: did I count anything twice?

scenes.chapter: Your turn: two rows of three

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now there are six lights, in two rows of three.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now there are six lights, in two rows of three.

lines.text: How many patterns have at least one full row, or at least one full column?
lines.caption: How many patterns have at least one full row, or at least one full column?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

scenes.chapter: Two rows of three: the answer

lines.text: Count the losers. Each row has seven safe choices. Seven times seven is forty-nine with no full row.
lines.caption: Count the losers. Each row has seven safe choices. Seven times seven is forty-nine with no full row.

lines.text: If column one is full, each row has three choices left. Three times three is nine.
lines.caption: If column one is full, each row has three choices left. Three times three is nine.

lines.text: Three columns give twenty-seven. Take away three with two full columns. That's twenty-four.
lines.caption: Three columns give twenty-seven. Take away three with two full columns. That's twenty-four.

lines.text: So the losers are forty-nine minus twenty-four, which is twenty-five.
lines.caption: So the losers are forty-nine minus twenty-four, which is twenty-five.

lines.text: There are two to the sixth, sixty-four patterns in all. Minus twenty-five is <short pause> thirty-nine!
lines.caption: There are two to the sixth, sixty-four patterns in all. Minus twenty-five is thirty-nine!

lines.text: The big idea: add the groups, subtract the pairs, add back the triples, and keep alternating.
lines.caption: The big idea: add the groups, subtract the pairs, add back the triples, and keep alternating.

lines.text: Then every pattern is counted exactly once. Or count the losers, and subtract from the total.
lines.caption: Then every pattern is counted exactly once. Or count the losers, and subtract from the total.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
